reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about nanosegregation behavior, its mechanical consequences, and mitigation strategies, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these key premises.
premises: Mechanical strain accelerates nanosegregation of Ni, Cr, Mn to grain boundaries in single-phase HEAs at elevated temperatures
This nanosegregation reduces grain boundary cohesion and causes intergranular brittle fracture
Preexisting Cr-rich precipitates at grain boundaries can act as sinks for embrittling elements
The untreated single-phase HEA baseline has minimal grain boundary segregation and high toughness at lower temperatures
The mechanism dominates at 400–700°C under dynamic/high strain-rate loading
